title: Mini Runway: rapid inference experiment runway (scratchpad)
content:
TL;DR:

A personal sketch for a lightweight, ephemeral feature runway ("Mini Runway") that lets engineers and PMs spin up small, isolated inference sandboxes to validate changes to model variants, batching policies, prefix caching, and quantization settings with minimal infra friction. Aim: get an actionable perf/cost/quality datapoint in <24h and turn winners into canary candidates for Dedicated/Hosted flows.

Motivation / problem space:
- Current experiment workflow is heavy: reserved capacity, infra requests, or asking SRE to carve out GPUs.
- By the time an idea has data, a lot of backlog/context leaks and the signal is stale.
- We need quick A/B style comparisons that include realistic multiplexing, small-batch latency, and prefix cache warmup dynamics.

What Mini Runway should enable (user stories):
- As an ML engineer, I want to run two model variants with identical prompt sets and traffic profile so I can measure latency and output divergence within a session-aware context.
- As a PM, I want to flip a quantization knob and see cost/cpu differences without touching Dedicated capacity or customers.
- As an SRE, I want ephemeral environments to validate autoscale policies and failure fallbacks without risking production configs.

Proposed high-level flow (UX + dev flow):
1) Quick form: name + model baseline + candidate model(s) + sample workload (upload .json or select saved prompt set) + desired token budget + duration (1h/6h/24h) + routing policy (latency-first / cost-first / mixed).
2) System provisions ephemeral routing policy tied to a small dedicated pool (cheap GPU small instance or CPU-backed emulator for very small tests).
3) Warmup phase: run prefix/kv caching warmup with synthetic sessions (optionally replay real telemetry via sanitized sample).
4) Run measurement: collect per-token latency, tail latency, token cost, generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity to baseline), hallucination markers if available.
5) Summarize result + exportable artifact (CSV + perf dashboard link) + option to promote candidate to a canary gate or save as an Optimize recommendation.

Minimum viable experiment matrix (what to vary):
- Model variant: baseline, smaller quantized, larger with sparsity, distilled variant
- Batch settings: small (1-2), medium (4-8), aggressive (16-32)
- Prefix caching: cold, warmed, warmed-with-eviction
- Max context / seq len: 512, 1024, 2048
- Routing policy: latency-priority vs cost-priority

Metrics to collect (automatic):
- Per-request: p50/p90/p99 latency (generation start, first token, end)
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec under target concurrency
- Cost: estimated per-1k-token cost and 24h extrapolation
- Quality: embedding-based similarity to baseline answers, token perplexity where available, simple heuristic checks (stops, repetition, hallucination keywords), and human-check flagging sample set for manual review
- Stability: error rates, OOMs, fallback invocations, model restarts

Success criteria (for a runway experiment being useful):
- End-to-end data in <24h with automated dashboard and CSV export.
- Clear delta on cost/latency/quality with at least one trusted metric (embedding similarity) and one operational metric (p99 latency).
- Promotion path: one-click to create a canary deployment config (reuses rollout policies) or add to Optimize suggestions.

Implementation notes / infra constraints:
- Use existing Dedicated sandbox infra with ephemeral nodes; if not available, fall back to lower-cost CPU emulation with caveat metrics.
- Instrumentation hooks: must reuse existing token-level tracing so results are comparable to hosted production.
- Storage: short-lived artifacts saved under user project (24–72h) with option to persist into product pipelines.
- Permissions: only low-risk datasets allowed; sensitive customer data must be scrubbed.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Cost control: who pays for the GPU minutes? charge back to requester by default? include a quota?
- Traffic realism: should we allow live traffic mirroring (hard security implications) or only replayed/synthetic?
- Metric trustworthiness: CPU-emulated runs will not match GPU perf—need clear labels and translation heuristics.
- Integration with Console: surface this as a card in model catalog or a separate DevX tool?

Short UX sketch (wireless words):
- Landing: "New runway experiment" CTA in DevX -> small modal with presets (fast smoke / realistic 1k tokens / throughput soak).
- Results page: three-column layout (summary + perf graphs + sample diffs). Highlight p99 delta and embedding similarity with color-coded pass/fail thresholds.
- Quick promote: button toggles a canary blueprint builder (copies traffic split, rollback window, and fallback model).

Safety / compliance checklist (quick):
- No PII allowed in sample datasets unless the user has Private deployment and KMS configured.
- Rate-limit experiments per user and per org to avoid noisy neighbors.

Next steps (for me):
- Prototype a clickable mock in Figma (assign to Ava).
- Mock minimal backend: small script to run two model instances and collect traces (Sam to spike).
- Paper design doc to product + infra (2–3p) to justify quota and chargeback model.
- Validate with 2 internal teams (Search team, Docs summarization) as pilot.

Notes to self / ideas to capture later:
- Option: pre-baked presets for common tactics (quantization-scan, batching-scan, cache-warmup).
- Idea: "experiment diff" artifact that can be attached to PRs (GH PR comment with summary) to make model-change reviews visible.
- Long-term: integrate with Optimize to recommend candidate profiles automatically based on experiment history.

Unresolved TODOs (short):
- Decide default quota and billing model.
- Draft security guardrails for live traffic mirroring.
- Skeleton API endpoints + GH PR surface design.
